graph.summary: Imatinib → Tyrosine-protein kinase ABL1 → leukocyte proliferation → Chronic Myeloid Leukemia

evidence.snippet: inhibiting oncogenic protein BCR::ABL1 in a targeted manner with imatinib, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor.
evidence.explanation: Imatinib is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor that targets and inhibits the oncogenic BCR::ABL1 kinase (whose catalytic domain is ABL1, UniProt:P00519), decreasing its activity in CML patients.

paper.title: Imatinib therapy of chronic myeloid leukemia significantly reduces carnitine cell intake, resulting in adverse events.

evidence.snippet: the inhibition of BCR-ABL1 kinase with Imatinib prevented Smad4 tyrosine phosphorylation and re-sensitized CML cells to TGF-β-induced antiproliferative and pro-apoptotic responses.
evidence.explanation: Imatinib inhibits BCR-ABL1 kinase activity, abolishing its downstream tyrosine-phosphorylation activity in CML cells — direct support for the decreases-activity-of edge.

paper.title: Imatinib blocks tyrosine phosphorylation of Smad4 and restores TGF-β growth-suppressive signaling in BCR-ABL1-positive leukemia.

evidence.snippet: generates the constitutively active BCR::ABL1 tyrosine kinase, driving uncontrolled myeloid proliferation.
evidence.explanation: The constitutively active BCR::ABL1 tyrosine kinase (ABL1 catalytic moiety, UniProt:P00519) drives uncontrolled myeloid (leukocyte) proliferation — i.e. it positively regulates the proliferation process.

paper.title: Importance of five membered heterocyclic compounds in treatment of chronic myeloid leukemia by targeting various pathways.

evidence.snippet: the dysregulated BCR-Abl fusion oncoprotein is formed and it produces the abnormal proliferation of white blood cells.
evidence.explanation: The BCR-Abl fusion kinase produces (positively regulates) the abnormal proliferation of white blood cells (leukocytes).

paper.title: Targeting BCR-Abl in the treatment of Philadelphia-chromosome positive chronic myelogenous leukemia.

evidence.snippet: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is a clonal hematopoietic malignancy characterized by the presence of the Philadelphia chromosome, which generates the constitutively active BCR::ABL1 tyrosine kinase, driving uncontrolled myeloid proliferation.
evidence.explanation: CML is defined as a malignancy characterized by uncontrolled myeloid (leukocyte) proliferation — the proliferative process is the defining cause/manifestation of the disease.

paper.title: Importance of five membered heterocyclic compounds in treatment of chronic myeloid leukemia by targeting various pathways.

evidence.snippet: Chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML) is driven by the t(9;22) forming the BCR::ABL1 fusion gene, leading to the development of hyper-myeloid proliferation.
evidence.explanation: CML development is characterized by hyper-myeloid proliferation, linking the leukocyte-proliferation process to the chronic myeloid leukemia disease state.

paper.title: Allosteric and ATP-Pocket BCR::ABL1 Inhibition In Vitro, and Characterising Ex Vivo Thrombo-Inflammatory Biomarkers and Thrombin Generation in Asciminib-Treated CML Patients.
